newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil sector sets record merger pace.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil sector sets record merger pace.

text.p: A gusher of funds available to Canadian oil and gas companies led to a record year for merger and acquisition activity in 1996, brokerage Sayer Securities Ltd said on Wednesday.
In a report, Sayer said the value of M&A transactions in Canada's energy business last year hit C$10.1 billion, up 35 percent from C$7.5 billion in 1995.
"The main catalyst for the increased demand for oil and gas assets was an increase in funds available to the industry," Sayer said. "Higher oil and gas prices led to increased production cash flows."
A record C$9.5 billion was raised in the Canadian oil patch in 1996 from equity offerings, debt issues and royalty trust financings.
Sayer said that the median price paid for oil and gas reserves last year was C$6.17 per barrel of oil equivalent, up from C$5.05 the year before.

Royalty trusts in 1996 contributed to the higher acquisition values by scooping up C$2 billion of assets at premium prices, Sayer said. Trusts, which use cash flow to pay out unit holders rather than invest in exploration, paid a median price of C$7.82 per BOE for assets, the brokerage said.
It said that the pace of M&A deals quickened last year as well and firms that served notice they were examining ways to "maximize shareholder value" were bought up with little hesitation.
"The stock market currently has little patience for exploration and production companies that are slow to show results," Sayer research manager Sarah Clayton said.
"Rightly or wrongly, the stock market does not hesitate to sell companies...that don't meet expectations."

With such recent deals as Gulf Canada Resources Ltd's C$1.4 billion takeover of Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc, the C$700 million merger of Northstar Energy Corp and Morrison Petroleums Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc's C$1.7 billion play for Wascana Energy Inc, 1997 is shaping up to be another banner year for corporate marriages in the sector.
